text: Rust allows only one mutable reference at a time so mutation stays exclusive and no other reference can read or write the same value while it changes. That rule prevents data races, the class of bugs where unsynchronized shared access includes at least one write and leads to undefined behavior.
thought:
The user is asking a conceptual question about Rust's borrow checker.

Rust enforces exclusive mutable access to prevent data races. This forbids aliasing and mutating the same value simultaneously.

This also prevents iterator invalidation and use-after-free bugs from aliased pointers.
